items.titleRaw: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
items.contentRaw: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53-7.38 dB across datasets while requiring lower training VRAM. We further ablate Hexels by showing that per primitive, Hexels outperform 2DGS by upto 4.74 dB while using lower training VRAM and having 2.31 times faster FPS. Even in unconstrained settings, Hexels offers complementary quality-memory trade-offs. For efficient 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% compared with memory-matched 2DGS across 15 DTU scans. On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, Hexels achieves the highest mean F1 among compared methods (34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS). We further also show that Hexels, as a general primitive, improves 2D image representation over Image-GS. Hexels push the Pareto frontier on the quality-efficiency trade-off of surface-aligned primitives.

payloadJson.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction

items.titleRaw: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
items.contentRaw: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

payloadJson.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning

items.titleRaw: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
items.contentRaw: Test-time adaptation helps a deployed model respond to changing inputs, but the same intervention can rescue one batch and damage the next. Updating normalization statistics, for example, can improve corrupted images yet fail when a batch contains mostly one class. Average accuracy hides these failures and cannot tell a model when to use an intervention. Target labels can guide this decision, but they are scarce and some choices are already clear. We introduce PORTAL, a controller that chooses when to deploy an intervention, which inputs to label, and when to stop querying. Each available prediction rule is a candidate, and its predictions are fixed before current feedback arrives. Every acquired label therefore evaluates all candidates on the same input. PORTAL combines these shared comparisons and directs queries toward candidates that can still overtake the current leader. It stops when the remaining labels cannot change the choice or when the possible accuracy gain no longer justifies another query. Our analysis links the required feedback to accuracy gaps and shared mistakes, explaining why some choices need much less evidence. Experiments show that this control turns an intervention that loses accuracy overall into a useful choice on selected batches. It prevents severe failures caused by changes in arrival order and preserves gains across complete corruption streams. When a fixed rule already works well, PORTAL uses little feedback to retain its performance. Periodic label checks reveal when past evidence needs refreshing and help the controller recover as conditions change. The acquired labels also train stronger candidates for future batches, and selection brings nearly all of their accuracy gains into deployment. The same feedback therefore improves both the choice made now and the predictions available to later batches.

payloadJson.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?

items.titleRaw: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
items.contentRaw: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following injected instructions. We evaluate HoS on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B. We compare it against SecAlign++, a state-of-the-art finetuning-based defense, and ASIDE, a defense that, like ours, builds instruction-data separation into the model architecture. We show that HoS offers greater robustness to adaptive attacks, better performance on standard utility benchmarks, and matches top performance on standard agentic prompt injection benchmarks. More specifically, the black-box RL-Hammer attack reaches 97% ASR against GPT-OSS-20B and 85% against SecAlign, but only 10% against HoS. Claudini, a state-of-the-art white-box attack, strengthened against HoS through autoresearch, requires 3 times more FLOPs to reach the same ASR on HoS as it does on GPT-OSS-20B or SecAlign. HoS preserves base-model utility across standard multiple-choice benchmarks and prompting setups, whereas SecAlign and ASIDE degrade in few-shot settings. On agentic benchmarks with static attacks, HoS and SecAlign perform similarly and substantially improve the security-utility trade-off over the base model. ASIDE struggles with tool use, achieving only 10% utility. These results show that prompt injection robustness can be achieved and improved through targeted attention interventions.

payloadJson.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness

items.titleRaw: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
items.contentRaw: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = Ψ(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $Ψ$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

payloadJson.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops

items.titleRaw: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
items.contentRaw: Atmospheric chemical mechanisms are commonly distributed in the language of the Kinetic PreProcessor (KPP), which generates efficient Fortran or C code but does not fit into the differentiable programming frameworks in which machine-learning models are developed. We present KPPax, a kinetic preprocessor that generates differentiable, just-in-time compiled, and vectorisable chemistry code in JAX from mechanisms written in the KPP language. KPPax evaluates the rate law with sparse operations in log space, which keeps it differentiable, and integrates the stiff system with the implicit solvers and the forward- and reverse-mode adjoints of the \texttt{diffrax} library, so that exact sensitivities are obtained without hand-derived adjoint code. We demonstrate two applications with the POLLU benchmark mechanism. In the first, the Fisher information matrix computed from an automatically differentiated Jacobian predicts, before any fit, which of the 25 rate coefficients a flow-tube-like design can identify, and noisy synthetic estimation confirms the predicted uncertainties of the nine identifiable rate coefficients to within about 30\% while revealing clusters of fast reactions of which only ratios are constrained. In the second, a neural-network correction of an emission inventory is trained offline on per-scenario 4D-Var retrievals and then fine-tuned online through the chemical model, which reduces the error of the biogenic correction by a factor of 2.4--5 and recovers information on low-temperature emissions that the individual retrievals lose. KPPax makes KPP mechanisms directly usable for parameter estimation and hybrid physics--machine-learning modelling.

payloadJson.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry

items.titleRaw: anthropics/claude-code v2.1.312 released
items.contentRaw:
## What's changed

- Added `oidc.user_id_claim` to the Claude apps gateway, to identify people by an id_token claim other than `sub`, such as Microsoft Entra ID's `oid`
- Added click to send: in fullscreen, clicking the "to send now" hint under a queued message sends it right away, as its key does
- Fixed managed settings and organization policy not being fetched for the rest of the session after signing in from the VS Code extension
- Fixed Claude overwriting a very large CLAUDE.md, rules file or @-included file in a subdirectory after seeing only its start; Write now asks Claude to read it all or edit in place
- Fixed per-directory and `paths:` skills not being found after a Bash `cd` deeper into a git repository
- Fixed a rare case where the first reply after resuming a session in the terminal could be missing the next time the session was resumed
- Fixed a command with an invalid name stopping all commands from loading, which could leave `claude -p` with no output
- Fixed the Read tool sometimes failing on PDF pages with "pdftoppm failed: Could not write image" when the clean-up of old session files ran at the same time
- Fixed the spinner, OpenTelemetry `effort` values and transcripts naming a newly picked effort level during a task before the model applied it; they now show the level in force
- Fixed the `/model` and `/effort` cache warning saying the re-read waits for your next message; a change made while Claude is working can trigger it sooner
- Fixed some sessions showing as waiting on you when the last message only mentioned items waiting on you mid-sentence
- Fixed agent view restoring input text on the next launch after it was cleared with Ctrl+C just before exiting
- Fixed agent view reopening in shell mode after exiting with Ctrl+D from an empty `!` input
- Fixed vim mode `d`, `c` and `y` with a `gj` or `gk` count larger than the lines left deleting or copying text; like Vim, they now only move the cursor
- Fixed `/verify` showing a long description meant for Claude in `/help` and the `/` command menu instead of a short one
- Improved the prompt's effort indicator: a change made mid-task now says it may wait for your next message, and the note clears when it no longer applies
- Improved WebFetch errors in cloud sessions: a host that does not resolve is now explained as possibly outside the allowed network domains, so Claude names the host to allow
- Changed Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and Mantle to use the shorter system prompt for model names Claude Code doesn't recognize, such as custom deployment names and inference profile ARNs, even when they front Sonnet or Haiku; set `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT=0` to keep the full prompt
- Changed automatic model switches after a flagged message to also cover model names Claude Code doesn't recognize, such as custom deployment names; set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_REFUSAL_FALLBACK=1` to turn them off
- Changed usage limit messages to call the 5-hour window the "5-hour limit" instead of the "session limit"
- Changed cloud sessions started from the CLI to get their names and branch names from the server
- Changed prompt and agent hooks to run at most 24 at a time per session, sub-agents included, plus at most 12 that have waited longer than their event's timeout; a `timeout` under 1 second now counts as 1 second
- Changed a subagent's `autoCompactWindow` to lower the window set by `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`, where it had no effect before; it still never raises that window
- Changed OpenTelemetry `mcp_server.name` to report the real name of fixed-URL remote MCP servers declared by plugins from the official Anthropic marketplace, instead of `custom`
- Changed Claude Code to stop sending the `claude_code.safety_event` OpenTelemetry event
- [VSCode] Fixed sessions ending on a bare exit code when your organization's settings couldn't be loaded or were refused at startup; the tab now says why and offers Retry or Sign in again
- [VSCode] Changed usage limit resets to show a clock time ("Resets at 3:10 PM") and to say "5-hour limit"
- [Cloud sessions] Added an effort level to the model picker when you create or edit a routine that runs in the cloud
- [Cloud sessions] Added a Bash editor with colors, line numbers and a Copy button to the setup script box in cloud environment settings
- [Cloud sessions] Improved the step shown when Claude adds a repository to a cloud session: opening it now shows a short table of what happened instead of raw JSON
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed resending an unchanged message after a failed send in a cloud session sometimes running it twice
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed a failed cloud environment creation showing its error only as a toast outside the open dialog; it now appears inside the dialog
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed Edit in a routine's menu on the Routines page going to the routine's page without opening its edit dialog
- [Remote Control] Fixed an unarchived Remote Control session showing as working until a computer reconnected; it now shows as idle
- [Claude Tag] Improved Claude Tag's retry notice in Slack to name the model in use, or say rate limits were hit, instead of a generic API error
- [Claude Tag] Fixed a Claude Tag channel's on/off switch and agent settings falling back to workspace defaults when an older private Slack channel goes public and gets a new ID
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack not replying in channels whose environment has network access set to None
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack sometimes posting a file in the wrong thread when it was answering in another thread of the same channel
- [Code Review] Fixed Code Review reviewing an outdated commit, or none at all, when GitHub delivered a push event late; it now reviews the pull request's current commit

- Fixed worktree-isolated sessions accepting some locale-prefixed commands the isolation guard should refuse
- Fixed worktree-isolated sessions on zsh accepting some arithmetic commands that the isolation guard should refuse
- Fixed worktrees and branch checkouts that Claude Code creates so they ignore git replace refs, as its other git operations already do
- Fixed profile store write protection not applying when the config directory is reached through a symlink
- Fixed sessions compacting repeatedly after reading files under a very large nested CLAUDE.md; a nested CLAUDE.md over the size limit now loads only its start
- Fixed ctrl+enter (send now) only queuing a message when pressed before the response had started, and restarting a prompt's hooks while leaving the message queued when pressed while those hooks were running
- Fixed key-bound slash commands running in the shell from `!` mode
- Fixed ctrl+o not showing messages from other agents and sessions that are still waiting to be delivered; they now appear in full under the transcript, marked as waiting
- Fixed long tool output previews being cut through an emoji, leaving session transcripts that `jq` could not parse
- Fixed Read reporting "File does not exist" for PDF page ranges in Linux sandboxes that share the parent's `/proc`

items.contentRaw: # Release v5.21.0 ## New Model additions ### MiniCPM-OCR MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/minicpm_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) * Feat test (#49920) by @guarin in [#49920](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49920) ### Flint Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/flint) * Add Flint model support. (#49824) by @lovishmadaan in [#49824](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49824) ### UltraVBert UltraVBert extends ModernVBert by pairing the UltraBERT text encoder with a SigLIP vision encoder for visual document understanding and retrieval. Its image processor splits each page into 512-pixel tiles plus a global view. The connector merges each 4 x 4 block of vision patches into one token, so a tile becomes 64 image tokens, and RMS-normalizes them to the scale of UltraBERT's token embeddings. The `max_image_tiles` setting (27 by default) caps the number of tiles per page. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultravbert) * Add UltraVBERT (#49685) by @athrael-soju in [#49685](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49685) ### Gradium Phonon TTS Gradium Phonon TTS is Gradium's family of on-device text-to-speech models, trained with the Pocket TTS recipe. A causal transformer reads a voice prompt and the text, then emits one continuous 32-dimensional audio latent per step at 12.5 Hz through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when the utterance ends. The latents are decoded to 24 kHz audio by a Pocket TTS audio tokenizer. Unlike Pocket TTS, voice conditioning uses 512-dimensional latents from a separate, unreleased speaker codec, so voices come as precomputed latents and cannot be cloned from a recording. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/gradium_phonon_tts) * Add GradiumPhononTTS (#49791) by @eustlb in [#49791](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49791) ### Pocket TTS Pocket TTS is Kyutai's 100M-parameter text-to-speech model, built as a Continuous Audio Language Model that runs faster than real time on CPU. A causal transformer emits one continuous audio latent per frame (12.5 Hz) through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when to stop. A Mimi-based audio tokenizer encodes voice prompts and decodes the generated latents to 24 kHz audio. Two flow heads are released, Lagrangian self-distillation (default) and drifting, and voices can be cloned from a recording, passed as precomputed latents, or loaded from cached KV states. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (the Continuous Audio Language Models paper, arXiv 2509.06926). It is the only paper the documentation links, and it describes the architecture family Pocket TTS belongs to. The docs do not cite a separate Pocket TTS technical report.) | [Blog Post](NONE. The documentation links no official blog post. It points only to the original code repository at https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts.) * add PocketTTS (#49589) by @eustlb in [#49589](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49589) ### Pocket TTS Audio Tokenizer The Pocket TTS audio tokenizer is the codec used by Pocket TTS. It has Mimi's architecture (SEANet convolutions plus a small causal transformer on each side), but its residual vector quantizer is replaced by a continuous 32-dimensional bottleneck, the VAE-GAN from Continuous Audio Language Models. It converts 24 kHz audio into latents at 12.5 Hz and decodes them back to audio. It serves as the `audio_tokenizer` of `PocketTTSProcessor`, encoding voice prompts and decoding generated latents, and its encoder and decoder can also be loaded on their own. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts_audio_tokenizer) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (Continuous Audio Language Models, whose VAE-GAN this tokenizer uses; arxiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06926)) * add PocketTTSAudioTokenizer (#49588) by @eustlb in [#49588](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49588) ## Breaking changes Fixed Gemma4 processor imports (the Gemma4, Gemma4 unified and EmbeddingGemma2 processors) so `from transformers import *` no longer fails in environments that have `PIL` but not `torch`; no user action is needed. * :rotating_light: Fix gemma4 cross imports resulting in import failing without `torch` but with `PIL` (#49748) by @Sai-Suraj-27 Added an `"fp8"` backend to `QuantizedCache`, alongside `quanto` and `hqq`, that stores KV states in `torch.float8_e4m3fn` with a single scale per tensor; enable it with `cache_implementation="quantized"` and `cache_config={"backend": "fp8"}`. * 🚨Add an FP8 backend to `QuantizedCache` (#48677) by @jiqing-feng Tensor parallelism now has a dedicated embedding style, shards every model's input embeddings by default, and supports widths that aren't divisible by the TP size, so `ColwiseParallel` and `RowwiseParallel` now apply only to linear layers; custom TP plans that applied them to embeddings must switch to the new embedding style. * 🚨 TP: give embeddings their own style, shard input embeddings by default, and shard widths that don't divide by the TP size (#49570) by @IlyasMoutawwakil Every MoE TP and EP plan now shards its experts, so models no longer keep all experts on every rank, and a new `test_moe_parallel_plans_shard_experts` test enforces this; custom or downstream MoE parallel plans must add expert sharding to pass it and to avoid wasted memory. * 🚨 MoE: shard the experts in every TP/EP plan, and test for it (#49206) by @IlyasMoutawwakil ## Cache This release improves cache handling across the library. release.body: # Release v5.21.0 ## New Model additions ### MiniCPM-OCR MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/minicpm_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) * Feat test (#49920) by @guarin in [#49920](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49920) ### Flint Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/flint) * Add Flint model support. (#49824) by @lovishmadaan in [#49824](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49824) ### UltraVBert UltraVBert extends ModernVBert by pairing the UltraBERT text encoder with a SigLIP vision encoder for visual document understanding and retrieval. Its image processor splits each page into 512-pixel tiles plus a global view. The connector merges each 4 x 4 block of vision patches into one token, so a tile becomes 64 image tokens, and RMS-normalizes them to the scale of UltraBERT's token embeddings. The `max_image_tiles` setting (27 by default) caps the number of tiles per page. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultravbert) * Add UltraVBERT (#49685) by @athrael-soju in [#49685](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49685) ### Gradium Phonon TTS Gradium Phonon TTS is Gradium's family of on-device text-to-speech models, trained with the Pocket TTS recipe. A causal transformer reads a voice prompt and the text, then emits one continuous 32-dimensional audio latent per step at 12.5 Hz through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when the utterance ends. The latents are decoded to 24 kHz audio by a Pocket TTS audio tokenizer. Unlike Pocket TTS, voice conditioning uses 512-dimensional latents from a separate, unreleased speaker codec, so voices come as precomputed latents and cannot be cloned from a recording. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/gradium_phonon_tts) * Add GradiumPhononTTS (#49791) by @eustlb in [#49791](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49791) ### Pocket TTS Pocket TTS is Kyutai's 100M-parameter text-to-speech model, built as a Continuous Audio Language Model that runs faster than real time on CPU. A causal transformer emits one continuous audio latent per frame (12.5 Hz) through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when to stop. A Mimi-based audio tokenizer encodes voice prompts and decodes the generated latents to 24 kHz audio. Two flow heads are released, Lagrangian self-distillation (default) and drifting, and voices can be cloned from a recording, passed as precomputed latents, or loaded from cached KV states. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (the Continuous Audio Language Models paper, arXiv 2509.06926). It is the only paper the documentation links, and it describes the architecture family Pocket TTS belongs to. The docs do not cite a separate Pocket TTS technical report.) | [Blog Post](NONE. The documentation links no official blog post. It points only to the original code repository at https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts.) * add PocketTTS (#49589) by @eustlb in [#49589](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49589) ### Pocket TTS Audio Tokenizer The Pocket TTS audio tokenizer is the codec used by Pocket TTS. It has Mimi's architecture (SEANet convolutions plus a small causal transformer on each side), but its residual vector quantizer is replaced by a continuous 32-dimensional bottleneck, the VAE-GAN from Continuous Audio Language Models. It converts 24 kHz audio into latents at 12.5 Hz and decodes them back to audio. It serves as the `audio_tokenizer` of `PocketTTSProcessor`, encoding voice prompts and decoding generated latents, and its encoder and decoder can also be loaded on their own. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts_audio_tokenizer) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (Continuous Audio Language Models, whose VAE-GAN this tokenizer uses; arxiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06926)) * add PocketTTSAudioTokenizer (#49588) by @eustlb in [#49588](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49588) ## Breaking changes Fixed Gemma4 processor imports (the Gemma4, Gemma4 unified and EmbeddingGemma2 processors) so `from transformers import *` no longer fails in environments that have `PIL` but not `torch`; no user action is needed. * :rotating_light: Fix gemma4 cross imports resulting in import failing without `torch` but with `PIL` (#49748) by @Sai-Suraj-27 Added an `"fp8"` backend to `QuantizedCache`, alongside `quanto` and `hqq`, that stores KV states in `torch.float8_e4m3fn` with a single scale per tensor; enable it with `cache_implementation="quantized"` and `cache_config={"backend": "fp8"}`. * 🚨Add an FP8 backend to `QuantizedCache` (#48677) by @jiqing-feng Tensor parallelism now has a dedicated embedding style, shards every model's input embeddings by default, and supports widths that aren't divisible by the TP size, so `ColwiseParallel` and `RowwiseParallel` now apply only to linear layers; custom TP plans that applied them to embeddings must switch to the new embedding style. * 🚨 TP: give embeddings their own style, shard input embeddings by default, and shard widths that don't divide by the TP size (#49570) by @IlyasMoutawwakil Every MoE TP and EP plan now shards its experts, so models no longer keep all experts on every rank, and a new `test_moe_parallel_plans_shard_experts` test enforces this; custom or downstream MoE parallel plans must add expert sharding to pass it and to avoid wasted memory. * 🚨 MoE: shard the experts in every TP/EP plan, and test for it (#49206) by @IlyasMoutawwakil ## Cache This release improves cache handling across the library. Flash Attention now works with static caches, BLOOM no longer crashes with static cache or compiled generate, chunked prefill supports cache continuation, and the Qwen4-Exp indexer's position history stays aligned with its cached keys. Linear-attention caches also gain new getters (`is_recording_past`, `get_recurrent_state`, conv-state access) that stop exposing cache internals and prepare for paged-c * [FA] Fix FA with static cache (#49998) by @Cyrilvallez in [#49998] * [docs] CB cache behavior (#49025) by @stevhliu in [#49025] * [CB] Reduce warmup time by not computing attention over full cache (#49853) by @remi-or in [#49853] * Fix Qwen4-Exp indexer position cache lifecycle (#49840) by @taking-lying-flat in [#49840] * [Cache] Linear attn cache: use new getters (#49375) by @remi-or in [#49375] * [Cache] Get conv states (#49309) by @remi-or in [#49309] * [Cache] Add get_recurrent_state (#49306) by @remi-or in [#49306] * [Cache] Add is_recording_past (#49305) by @remi-or in [#49305] * Fix BLOOM crash with static cache / compiled generate (#49481) by @kaixuanliu in [#49481] * Allow Cache continuation for chunked prefill (#49662) by @Cyrilvallez in [#49662] ## Vision Vision image processors now composite PNG transparency onto white instead of exposing black pixels, and `background_color` is preserved correctly across the DeepSeek-VL and Janus processors. items.contentRaw: # Release v5.20.0 ## New Model additions ### Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/muse_spark) | [Blog Post](http://hf.co/blog/meta-muse-spark-open) * Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in [#49644](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49644) ### Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so it loads without `trust_remote_code=True`. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/bailing_hybrid) * [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in [#49446](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49446) ### Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism. * :rotating_light: SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as `` as special tokens (not split, honored by `skip_special_tokens`, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. It also speeds up Whisper generation on TPU by cutting device syncs and recompilation, and fixes Whisper batched timestamp decoding for tensor and NumPy inputs. Pipelines get a cleanup of generation-argument handling that removes spurious warnings. * Add job to automatically generate Intel CPU Docker image (#49560) by @regisss in [#49560] * Image decoding moves to torchcodec (#47963) by @zucchini-nlp in [#47963] * Optimize Whisper generation for TPU and device sync (#49426) by @tengomucho in [#49426] * Generation cleanup in pipelines (#49269) by @Rocketknight1 in [#49269] * Fix Whisper batch timestamp decoding for tensors (#49419) by @Kingofbooks in [#49419] ## Vision Vision processing was updated in several places. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/kolibri1) * Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in [#49463](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49463) ### MiniCPM-V 4.7 [MiniCPM-V](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by [OpenBMB](https://github.com/OpenBMB). Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is *canvas M-RoPE*: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a `(temporal, height, width)` position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. * Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in [#48979](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48979#top) ### UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/unlimited_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.23050 (the docs link only the Hugging Face papers page, "Unlock OCR Works" is not given an arXiv link, so this is the paper URL provided)) * Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in [#46836](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46836) ### UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultrabert) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.15028) * Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in [#49596](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49596) ### MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as `[start][S01]text[end]`. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/moss_transcribe_diarize) * Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in [#48386](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48386) ## Breaking changes 🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨 Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from `cache_utils.py` (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API. * 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead. * 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin The minimum `kernels` version is now 0.17.2, which allows `use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL` so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade `kernels` to 0.17.2 or later. * 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc A new `SubConfigSpec` centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism. * :rotating_light: SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as `` as special tokens (not split, honored by `skip_special_tokens`, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. Tokenization and decoding output involving these tokens may therefore differ from before, so check any code or saved outputs that depend on the old behavior. * 🚨🚨🚨 luke fixe (#48408) by @itazap ## Exporters Transformers exporters now support quantization directly during export across Dynamo, ONNX, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. This makes it easier to export optimized models for efficient inference across different backends. For more information see the docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/exporters_quantization ## Parallelization This release improves distributed training and inference. FSDP × TP model and optimizer checkpoints can now be saved and loaded across different parallel configurations, and expert-parallel dispatch, tensor-parallel plans, static-cache `generate()`, and the caching allocator's byte count were fixed. Tied LM heads in composite models now get their own TP plan entry, `enable_expert_parallel` applies the EP plan alone again, TPU loading uses the `tor * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading, Optimizer (#49256) by @michaelbenayoun in [#49256] * FSDP x TP Saving / Loading (#48802) by @michaelbenayoun in [#48802] * Don't set a device per rank for gloo tensor-parallel tests (#49636) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49636] * fix(distributed): keep enable_expert_parallel as EP alone (#49633) by @dacorvo in [#49633] * Fix a port allocation race in FSDP tests (#49455) by @icavan in [#49455] * Expert-parallel dispatch hands the experts the received rows, not the all-to-all's pending result (#49421) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49421] * Fix static-cache generate() with host-side inputs and under TP (#49317) by @dacorvo in [#49317] * Composite lm head tp plan (#49080) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49080] * Fix: use torch.accelerator device APIs so TP loading works again on TPU (#49502) by @tengomucho in [#49502] * Count ep and fsdp in caching_allocator_warmup byte calculation (#49384) by @3outeille in [#49384] * Do not wrap the model in FSDP for expert-parallel token dispatch (#49383) by @3outeille in [#49383] ## Generation This release fixes static-cache `generate()` bugs with host-side inputs and under tensor parallelism. ## Liquid AI LFM3

[LFM3](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3) is Liquid AI's new family of small models built for local agents, tool calling, and structured output, on Liquid's new tri-hybrid architecture. The family includes:

- [lfm3](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3): a 1.7B text model with a 256K-token context window
- [lfm3-vl](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-vl): adds image understanding
- [lfm3-audio](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-audio): speech recognition, translation, and text-to-speech in 18 languages
- [lfm3-omni](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-omni): text, images, and audio in one model

```sh
ollama run lfm3
```

## d1 decision models

Liquid AI's d1 models now come in a 2B size, built on LFM3. [d1](https://ollama.com/library/d1) makes decisions about text and images, and [d1-omni](https://ollama.com/library/d1-omni) adds audio.

```sh
ollama run d1:2b "I was charged twice for order 4417." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
```

Note: lfm3 and d1 2b are supported on Apple hardware in this release.  Support for Linux/Windows coming soon.

## What's Changed
- Faster prompt processing on Apple silicon for Gemma 4, Flint and Laguna models
- Speculative decoding now supports DFlash2 draft models on MLX
- Gemma 4 keeps more detail in small images
- `ollama launch` now works with OpenCode v2
- Fixed tool-only assistant turns from Kimi CLI
- Updated MLX and llama.cpp

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.11...v0.40.12

Ollama can now generate [speech](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/speech) on macOS. `ollama run` plays text or a chat model's reply aloud as the audio is generated, and apps can stream audio through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint.

ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama."

ollama run d3 "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"

items.titleRaw: Show HN: AgentState – Lightweight state manager for multi-agent AI workflows
items.contentRaw:
AgentState to solve a problem I kept running into: managing state for multi-agent AI systems is surprisingly hard. When you have multiple AI agents that need to coordinate, persist their state, and query each other's status, you typically end up with a mess of Redis/Postgres setups, custom queuing, and manual synchronization code.

The whole thing is ~3MB, written in Rust for performance and safety, runs in Docker, and handles 1000+ ops/sec. I've been running it in production for AI workflows and it's been rock solid.

items.titleRaw: Show HN: ML Blocks – Deploy multimodal AI workflows without code
items.contentRaw:
Hey everyone,

ML Blocks is a node-based workflow builder to create multi-modal AI workflows without writing any code.

You connect blocks that call various visual models like GPT4v, Segment Anything, Dino etc. along with basic image processing blocks like resize, invert color, blur, crop, and several others.

The idea is to make it easier to deploy multi-step image processing workflows, without needing to spin up endless custom OpenCV cloud functions to glue together AI models. Usually, even if you're using cloud inference servers like Replicate, you still need to write your own image processing code to pre and post-process images in your pipeline. When you're trying to move fast, that's just unnecessary overhead.

With ML Blocks, you can build a workflow and deploy the whole thing as a single API. AFAIK, ML Blocks is the only end-to-end workflow builder built specifically for image processing.

If you're curious, our models run on Replicate, HuggingFace & Modal Labs cloud GPUs and we use React Flow for the node UX.
